editorial:
Imagine waking up in a hospital bed after trying to end it all, only to find that your messy personal life has finally caught up with you. That is exactly what happens to Sandro Lanza, a failed actor who has spent years avoiding his responsibilities. The story kicks off when his three daughters, who have never really known each other and live all over Europe, are forced to come home. You get to watch these three strangers navigate their shared anger and sadness while trying to figure out if they can even forgive their father. The vibe is a mix of a sad family drama and a quirky comedy, making it feel like a real conversation between people who don't know how to talk to each other.

You will really love how the acting feels natural and not over the top. The way the sisters slowly bond is the best part of the whole experience, though the pacing can feel a bit slow in the middle. If you enjoy stories about broken families finding a way back to each other, you should definitely give this a shot. It is a great pick to stream in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality, or you could just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy movie night. If you are a fan of collecting physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a solid move.
endingExplained: In the end, the daughters stop fighting and realize they have more in common with each other than they do with their father. Instead of leaving him to suffer, they find a way to accept him despite his many flaws. The movie wraps up with a sense of peace as the sisters form a real bond. They move past the trauma and decide to be a family, giving their father a second chance at life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves touching family stories and character studies.
